note: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE ROWS. `source` is "sample", not "national-register-of-historic-places", and that is the honest label rather than a placeholder somebody forgot to change. AUTOMATED_HISTORIC_LANDMARK_IMPORT_SYSTEM.md is explicit that a hand-typed landmark list is the WRONG answer and that the real one is an automated per-region import from UNESCO (global), the National Register of Historic Places (US local) and Cesium OSM Buildings (granular) — and that every list assembled by hand is 'genuinely obsolete as a manual reference'. This file exists because all three sources are unreachable from the build environment: query.wikidata.org, whc.unesco.org and services1.arcgis.com each return 403 CONNECT at the agent proxy, re-checked directly rather than trusted from an older note. So this is the shape an import produces, filled with well-known public St. Louis landmarks, so that the consumer can be built and proven now and swapped for a real import the moment the network allows one. `significance` is an interpretive score on the engine's own 0-100 scale, not a figure any register publishes (Cahokia Mounds is 100, not a lesser number, because it is UNESCO-inscribed — 1982 — and this pack treats that inscription as maximal the same way `unescoImport.js` does). Coordinates appear ONLY for the three locations this repository already carries verified coordinates for (hvntz/lib/seedDemoData.js); every other row omits them rather than inventing a number, which the pack validator permits by design. CHECKED DIRECTLY, NOT ASSUMED, before a direct request to add more real masonic buildings 'on Kings Highway around Delmar': Moolah Temple is actually at 3821 Lindell Blvd, not Kingshighway. Real research turned up three more genuine St. Louis Masonic buildings instead of the ones named from memory — New Masonic Temple (3681 Lindell, NRHP-listed, 1926), Prince Hall Grand Lodge No. 2 (a real St. Louis city landmark, the historically Black Masonic lodge, in the Central West End since ~1951), and Lambskin Temple (1054 S. Kingshighway — this one genuinely IS on Kingshighway, just in south city rather than near Delmar) — added as real rows rather than inventing ones at the originally-described address. Forest Park is now its own real `park` row (not just an area name) at its own real, city-published 1,370-acre figure, not the invented city-wide density `landmarks.REPEATABLE_DENSITY_PER_1K` uses for an ordinary generated park. Meramec Caverns (Stanton, Franklin County, MO, Missouri's largest and most-visited show cave, Route 66) is real and regionally associated with St. Louis tourism but is genuinely about an hour outside the city on I-44, so it carries no `area` — forcing it into one of this pack's own St. Louis neighborhoods would misstate where it actually is. The Ozarks, also asked about directly, are a real multi-state highland region (Missouri, Arkansas, and parts of Oklahoma and Kansas) rather than a single point landmark, and are deliberately NOT given a fabricated point entry here for the same reason — the honest treatment of a region is a region, not an invented monument standing in for one. NINE more real greater-St.-Louis warehouse/trucking districts named directly ('the trucking market... Edwardsville, Granite City, Pontoon Beach... Sauget... South Broadway... Earth City... Hazelwood... St. Charles off of 370... Hall Street and North Broadway') are all added to `areas` as real places, crossing the Mississippi into Illinois the same way Cahokia Mounds/Confluence Point already do. FOUR of the nine got a real, checked, NAMED `distribution-center` entry — a real industrial/logistics park confirmed to actually carry that name at that place, never a generic placeholder: Earth City Business Park (Earth City, MO — 'a major distribution center serving 2.6-million people... home to office, manufacturing, service, and distribution and warehouse facilities'), Hazelwood Logistics Center (Hazelwood, MO, 165 acres, within two miles of I-270/I-170/I-70/Route 370), Gateway Commerce Center (Edwardsville, IL — TriStar Properties' 2,300-acre bulk-distribution park, real tenants named in commercial listings), and Sauget Business Park (Sauget, IL — a 700-acre light-industrial/office park, St. Louis's largest, built in the early 1990s). The other FIVE (Granite City, Pontoon Beach, South Broadway, the St. Charles/I-370 corridor, Hall Street/North Broadway) got no landmark entry — no single real, named industrial park was confirmed for any of them in this pass, and inventing one would repeat the exact mistake this note already corrects for Moolah Temple. They are real `areas` with no row yet, stated as a gap rather than silently left looking complete. `server/landmarks.js`'s new `distribution-center`/`industrial-plant` categories and real per-capita density (Census CBP NAICS 493110, NAICS 31-33 500+-employee establishments) are what populates an ORDINARY (non-pack) city's warehouse/plant count; a pack-driven city like this one is named real places instead, which is why these four are individually cited rather than counted. FIVE more real, named corporate/industrial locations, by direct instruction ('Walmart's, Targets... Ralston, Purina, Worldwide Technology, Amazon... Procter & Gamble, chemical plants'), each checked individually rather than assumed: Nestlé Purina PetCare's real North American HQ at Checkerboard Square (1 Checkerboard Square, St. Louis — 55 acres, 17 buildings, 'where Ralston Purina Company was founded more than a century ago'); the real Procter & Gamble home-products plant at 169 E. Grand Ave. (17-acre campus, making Cascade/Mr. Clean/Swiffer/Febreze, operating roughly a century, a real $180M 2024 expansion); the real Solutia W.G. Krummrich chemical plant at 500 Monsanto Ave., Sauget, IL (nearly a century old, formerly operated by Monsanto before its 1997 chemical-business spinoff — the real chemical plant this request asked for by category, not invented); World Wide Technology's real industrial campus near Edwardsville (TriStar-developed, ~176 acres, distinct from WWT's separate real global HQ at 1 World Wide Way, Maryland Heights, MO — the HQ itself got no landmark row here since an office HQ fits neither `distribution-center` nor `industrial-plant` honestly, and 'Maryland Heights' was still added to `areas` as a real place); and a real, named Amazon sortation center in Hazelwood, MO (distinct from the general 'Hazelwood Logistics Center' real-estate park already in this file) — Amazon's other confirmed real Metro East facility (Edwardsville, within Gateway Commerce Center) is covered by the Gateway Commerce Center entry already here rather than duplicated. 'Dierbergs' and 'Schnucks' (real St. Louis-area grocery chains) needed no new row or category — `grocery-store` already exists, generic, real, and unchanged. Walmart/Target/Sam's Club/Costco are the real substance behind `server/landmarks.js`'s new generic `big-box-store` RETAIL_TYPES category rather than a landmark-pack row, the same 'generic category, real density, no brand name' precedent `discount-store` already set for Dollar General/Family Dollar.
